court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction under §1252
issues.why: The court must confirm it has statutory jurisdiction to review the final removal order and any limits on reviewability.

issues.label: Exhaustion of administrative remedies
issues.why: The court must determine which arguments were properly raised to the BIA and are therefore preserved for judicial review.

issues.label: Final agency action identification
issues.why: The court must identify whether the BIA opinion, IJ opinion, or both constitute the reviewable agency reasoning.

issues.label: Standard of review framework
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards (substantial evidence vs de novo) to factual findings, legal questions, and mixed questions.

issues.label: Scope of record and factfinding bar
issues.why: The court must decide the petition on the administrative record and avoid impermissible appellate factfinding.

issues.label: Credibility finding effect
issues.why: Because the IJ found credibility, the court must treat the factual narrative as accepted absent legal error.

issues.label: Past persecution legal sufficiency
issues.why: The court must assess whether threats/abuse described constitute past persecution under the INA.

issues.label: Future persecution objective reasonableness
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the record compels a well-founded fear/clear probability of future persecution.

issues.label: Persecutor identity and attribution
issues.why: The court must consider whether harm by the father and masked men qualifies as persecution by a non-state actor requiring inability/unwillingness to protect.

issues.label: Nexus requirement—general
issues.why: Asylum/withholding require showing a protected ground was at least one central reason (asylum) or a reason (withholding) for the harm.

issues.label: Personal vendetta vs protected ground
issues.why: The court must distinguish retaliation for accusations/investigation from persecution on account of a protected characteristic.

issues.label: Political opinion definition
issues.why: The court must decide whether “opposition to violence/rule of law” can constitute a cognizable political opinion in this context.

issues.label: Political opinion—actual or imputed
issues.why: The court must assess whether the applicant held or was perceived to hold the asserted political opinion.

issues.label: Political opinion nexus to threats
issues.why: The court must determine whether evidence compels that the father/associates threatened her because of that opinion rather than to silence her.

issues.label: PSG cognizability—legal test
issues.why: The court must apply immutability, particularity, and social distinction to each proposed PSG.

issues.label: PSG 'females viewed as property'
issues.why: The court must assess whether this group is defined with sufficient particularity/social distinction and not circularly by harm.

issues.label: Gender-based nexus evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether the record compels that gender or property-like status motivated the persecution.

issues.label: PSG 'Salvadoran women' cognizability
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether this broad group satisfies particularity/social distinction under circuit/BIA law.

issues.label: PSG 'Salvadoran women' preservation
issues.why: The court must decide whether this PSG was properly raised before the IJ or was forfeited when first emphasized on appeal.

issues.label: Family PSG cognizability
issues.why: The court must consider whether the nuclear family of Porfiria Paz is a cognizable PSG under prevailing precedent.

issues.label: Family PSG nexus analysis
issues.why: The court must determine whether harm was because of membership in that family unit or for another non-protected reason.

issues.label: Mixed motives and central reason
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether family relationship was at least one central reason even if retaliation/silencing also motivated the persecutor.

issues.label: Witness-related PSG membership
issues.why: The court must decide whether the applicant/derivative qualifies as a member of any witness-based PSG given the record.

issues.label: Witness-related PSG cognizability
issues.why: The court must address whether “family members of prosecutorial witnesses” (or witnesses to crime) meets PSG requirements.

issues.label: Witness PSG preservation/waiver
issues.why: The court must determine whether newly framed PSGs raised to the BIA but not the IJ were properly declined as unpreserved.

issues.label: Alternative relief: withholding INA
issues.why: The court must apply the higher likelihood standard and correct nexus standard for statutory withholding if asylum fails.

issues.label: Asylum eligibility vs discretion
issues.why: If eligibility were established, the court must recognize asylum is discretionary while withholding is mandatory.

issues.label: Derivative asylum for J.P.A.
issues.why: The court must apply derivative-asylum rules and confirm the derivative claim rises or falls with the principal’s asylum grant.

issues.label: Derivative status limits for withholding/CAT
issues.why: The court must note that withholding/CAT do not provide derivative benefits, affecting any relief for J.P.A.

issues.label: CAT legal definition of torture
issues.why: The court must determine whether feared harm meets the severity and intent requirements for 'torture' under CAT regulations.

issues.label: CAT probability standard
issues.why: The court must apply the 'more likely than not' standard to future torture risk.

issues.label: CAT government acquiescence standard
issues.why: The court must apply the correct definition of acquiescence, including willful blindness and breach of legal duty.

issues.label: CAT state action/instigation
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether any public official would instigate, consent, or acquiesce to torture by private actors.

issues.label: Evidence of governmental inability/unwillingness
issues.why: The court must assess whether investigative failures, corruption, or inaction compel a finding of acquiescence (CAT) or inability/unwillingness (asylum/withholding).

issues.label: Significance of open investigation
issues.why: The court must decide what weight to give that the murder investigation remained open despite limited steps taken.

issues.label: Country conditions relevance
issues.why: The court must consider documentary country evidence on domestic violence, impunity, and witness intimidation in El Salvador as it bears on nexus and state protection/acquiescence.

issues.label: Internal relocation feasibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether the applicant could avoid harm by relocating within El Salvador and who bears the burden for relocation.

issues.label: Government protection adequacy
issues.why: The court must assess whether seeking help from police was required or futile and whether the state would protect her from her father/associates.

issues.label: Past persecution presumption mechanics
issues.why: If past persecution is found, the court must apply the regulatory presumptions and rebuttal rules for future persecution/relocation.

issues.label: BIA adoption/affirmance adequacy
issues.why: The court must ensure the BIA provided sufficient reasoning and properly adopted the IJ without overlooking material issues.

issues.label: BIA procedural handling of new PSGs
issues.why: The court must decide whether the BIA correctly declined to reach PSGs raised for the first time on appeal.

issues.label: Material evidence consideration
issues.why: The court must determine whether the agency ignored or mischaracterized evidence (e.g., threats by masked men, police conduct) such that remand is required.

issues.label: Legal error vs factual disagreement
issues.why: The court must separate alleged misapplications of law (reviewable) from challenges to factual weighing (deferential).

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: If any agency error is identified, the court must decide whether it was prejudicial or harmless.

issues.label: Remedy and remand scope
issues.why: If the petition is granted, the court must determine the proper disposition (remand for further proceedings vs partial relief).
